issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse visibility differs across artifacts. The UML in problem_statement.md declares singFarmSongVerse as private (UML member: "- singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal):void"), and the template implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java defines a private helper method (signature: "private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)" at the template). The solution implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares the method as protected (signature: "protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)"). This inconsistency can confuse students about the intended access level (whether the verse helper is intended to be a private internal helper or accessible to subclasses/tests) and may cause mismatched expectations in tests or when extending the class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent across artifacts. Either (a) change the solution's singFarmSongVerse declaration to private to match the UML and the template (i.e., "private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)"), or (b) update the UML in problem_statement.md and the template to indicate protected if the method is intentionally meant to be accessible to subclasses/tests. After choosing one option, ensure all three locations (problem statement UML, template Farm.java, and solution Farm.java) use the same visibility and update any tests or documentation accordingly.
